hero.title: Control Flow
intro.0: How code decides and repeats. Each of these six builds takes one control-flow tool - if/else, boolean logic, while, for, foreach with break/continue, switch - and asks for a small working method. The pattern is shown above each card; you fill in the body and run it.
task.1.title: Branch with if / else
task.1.context: An `if` / `else if` / `else` chain picks exactly one branch, top to bottom. The pattern below sorts a temperature into bands; do the same to turn an error count into a level.
task.1.goal.0: Return `"critical"` when errors is 10 or more, `"warn"` when it is 1 or more, otherwise `"clean"`.
task.1.goal.1: errors is 3 here, so the output should be warn.
task.2.title: Combine conditions
task.2.context: `&&` is true only when both sides are, `||` is true when either side is, and `!` flips a bool. The pattern below mixes all three; do the same to decide access.
task.2.goal.0: Return `"allow"` when the user is a `member` or `age` is 18+, and is not `banned`; otherwise `"deny"`.
task.2.goal.1: Here age is 20 and not banned, so the output should be allow.
task.3.title: Repeat with while
task.3.context: A `while` loop repeats while its condition holds. Step the counter with `n--` each pass or it never ends. The pattern below counts down; do the same, then print `liftoff`.
task.3.goal.0: Print `count`, then `count - 1`, down to 1, then print `"liftoff"`.
task.3.goal.1: From 3 the output is four lines: 3, 2, 1, liftoff.
task.4.title: Count with for
task.4.context: A `for` loop gives you an index, so you can number items or reach positions. The header is `for (start; condition; step)` and `i++` advances the index. Do the same to number each item.
task.4.goal.0: Print each item with its 1-based position, like `"1. login"`.
task.4.goal.1: For login then logout the output is: 1. login then 2. logout.
task.5.title: Skip and stop with foreach
task.5.context: Inside a `foreach`, `continue` jumps to the next item and `break` ends the loop. The pattern below prints lines, skipping blanks and stopping at `END`; do the same with skip and stop.
task.5.goal.0: Walk the steps: `continue` past a `"skip"`, `break` at a `"stop"`, otherwise print the step.
task.5.goal.1: For a, skip, b, stop, c the output is just: a then b.
task.6.title: Map values with switch
task.6.context: A `switch` maps one value to many cases; each `case` ends with `break` and `default` catches the rest. Here you run a switch for every item with a `foreach`. Do the same to label each code.
task.6.goal.0: For each code print a word: 1 -> `"low"`, 2 -> `"mid"`, 3 -> `"high"`, anything else -> `"?"`.
task.6.goal.1: For 1, 3, 9 the output is: low, high, ?.
concept.pr-conditional.def: Choosing exactly one branch to run by testing conditions, top to bottom.
concept.pr-loop.def: Repeating a block of code - with while, for, or foreach - and steering it with break and continue.
concept.pr-switch.def: Mapping one value to many cases, each ending in break, with default catching the rest.
